summary_en: Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu raised FY2027 March year-end dividend by 5 yen to 50 yen per share, with full-year dividend projected at 95 yen, reflecting stronger-than-expected passenger demand and robust vehicle sales.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Operating Forecast and Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu announced on October 29, 2026, a revision to its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The company increased its year-end dividend projection from 45 yen to 50 yen per share, resulting in a full-year dividend of 95 yen per share, up from the previously forecast 90 yen. The second quarter interim dividend remains at 45 yen. This 5-yen increase to the year-end dividend was decided based on recent business performance and financial condition. The company raised its full-year net income forecast to 4,150 million yen from 3,730 million yen, reflecting stronger operating results.

The upward revision to earnings and dividends was driven by two main factors: first, passenger demand in the bus and coach business exceeded initial expectations; second, the automobile sales business performed robustly, with high-priced vehicles such large trucks and vehicle maintenance services generating strong revenues. Despite recording losses from business restructuring in other segments, consolidated net income attributable to parent company shareholders is now expected to exceed the previous forecast.

The company operates under a basic dividend policy targeting a consolidated payout ratio of 30 percent and a consolidated net assets dividend rate of 2 percent, aiming for stable shareholder distributions while maintaining internal reserves necessary for business investment and management flexibility.
